proposals.citation: dedr[entry 1187];varghese-mathew2015idukki[Appendix B3, item 28, Mala Pulaya, Dendukombu]
proposals.evidence: DEDR1187 gives Tamil katavu/katavam and Malayalam katavu/kataku ‘door’, with Kannada kadavu. The selected southern survey kata-vɨ/kaḍavu-type simple door responses are comparative lect extensions; source spacing, voicing and final-vowel notation remain unchanged. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

These Mannan, Mala Pulaya and Irula simple roof responses are comparative lect extensions of that family; the survey vowel lengths and endings remain unchanged. The primary question mark concerns Kolami kuroḍi, not the southern comparanda. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.citation: dedr[entry 156];varghese-mathew2015idukki[Appendix B3, item 105, Mala Pulaya, Dendukombu]
proposals.evidence: DEDR156(a) gives Tamil appaṉ, Malayalam appan, Kannada appa and Kodagu appë father. The selected survey appa/appan/appe responses retain the same locally elicited father sense; minority-lect extensions are comparative. This nursery/honorific family does not by itself distinguish shared inheritance from regional diffusion, and other languages’ mother/aunt senses are not substituted. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.citation: dedr[entry 2248];varghese-mathew2015idukki[Appendix B3, item 87, Mala Pulaya, Dendukombu]
proposals.evidence: DEDR2248 gives Tamil/Malayalam kōḻi fowl, Kota kōy, Kodagu kōḷi, Kannada kōḻi and Tulu kōri/kōḷi. These southern survey kōyi/koyɨ/kōḷi/kośi/kojī-type responses are comparative lect extensions, retaining the glide, lateral and palatal/sibilant variants. The source chicken sense is compatible with fowl; this does not merge them with the distinct central-Dravidian kor family. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.citation: dedr[entry 4798];varghese-mathew2015idukki[Appendix B3, item 89, Mala Pulaya, Dendukombu]
proposals.evidence: DEDR4798 gives Tamil/Malayalam māṭu ox and Kota māṛ beast, explicitly including cattle and buffalo. The southern survey maḍɨ/maḍu cow responses are comparative lect extensions of this cattle term, with a more specific female-bovine elicitation gloss than the Tamil/Malayalam ox gloss. Preserve that semantic difference and all original vowel-length/voicing notation. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
